title: Typicality of entanglement growth and transport fluctuations in quantum symmetric exclusion processes
abstract: We use macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT) to establish the typicality of charge-transfer statistics and entanglement dynamics in the quantum symmetric exclusion process, a model of stochastically hopping free fermions with diffusive transport and long-range quantum coherence. We show that the leading long-time charge-transfer full counting statistics of individual noise realizations coincide almost surely with those of the classical symmetric exclusion process (SSEP), in equilibrium and following quenches from arbitrary occupation-diagonal product states. Our results apply to transient fluctuations in the thermodynamic limit, extending previous work that has primarily focused on stationary regimes. Our approach compares the noise averages of the charge-transfer generating function and its inverse. The former reduces to SSEP, while the latter maps to an auxiliary Brownian energy process whose MFT saddle-point problem is related to that of SSEP, yielding matching large-deviation exponents. Through free-fermion identities relating entanglement to subsystem-number fluctuations, this establishes the self-averaging of the covariance-matrix eigenvalue distribution and of Rényi and von Neumann entropies. We obtain asymptotically exact predictions for entanglement growth from domain-wall and Néel initial states, in excellent agreement with numerical simulations.
summary: This theoretical work proves that the complex quantum dynamics of the Quantum Symmetric Exclusion Process (QSSEP) are governed by the statistics of its classical counterpart, the SSEP, even during transient evolution. Using Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory, the authors establish the typicality of entanglement growth and charge-transfer fluctuations. This provides powerful, analytically derived predictions for quantum entanglement in integrable many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper establishes the typicality of charge-transfer statistics and entanglement dynamics in the quantum symmetric exclusion process (QSSEP) in the transient regime following quenches.
main_result: It proves that the long-time charge-transfer statistics of the QSSEP almost surely coincide with those of the classical symmetric exclusion process (SSEP), yielding asymptotically exact predictions for entanglement growth.
method: The analysis heavily employs Macroscopic Fluctuation Theory (MFT) and techniques involving the comparison of forward and inverse generating functions to establish convergence to classical limits.
model_or_system: The system is the Quantum Symmetric Exclusion Process (QSSEP), a model of stochastically hopping free fermions exhibiting diffusive transport and long-range quantum coherence. Its classical counterpart is the SSEP.
key_observables: Charge-transfer full counting statistics, Rényi and von Neumann entropies, and the subsystem covariance matrix eigenvalue distribution.
important_parameters: The analysis focuses on the transient regime, large time limits ($t 	o \infty$), and the diffusive scaling $\ell \equiv \sqrt{Dt}$.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on comparing the noise averages of the generating function and assuming the dominant saddles in the MFT are smoothly connected to the zero-tilt solutions.
figures_summary: Figures compare entanglement predictions and rescaled eigenvalue counts for domain-wall and Néel states, showing excellent agreement between analytical SSEP predictions and numerical simulations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing typicality using MFT by comparing forward and inverse generating functions, then extending this proof to the complex field domain using spectral bounds, and finally deriving the asymptotic form for the von Neumann entropy.
why_interesting: The rigorous connection between quantum entanglement dynamics (entropy growth) and classical stochastic processes (SSEP) via typicality arguments is highly relevant for understanding non-equilibrium quantum many-body physics.
